purpose: Teach: 釜/両替/酸性/バニラ/ともだち/オールスター/ジャイアンツ/ペラペラ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、お釜、絶対、ご飯、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — when you were young, I remember how much you truly loved your father. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward in time. Gentle conviction on the memory itself. Warm but tentative, as if asking permission to speak it aloud. Slow exhale at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、銀行で、絶対、両替、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、よく、絶対、行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When you were young, I remember how often you'd go to the bank to change money with your grandfather. You remember that, don't you dear?
lines.style: Matching his pace. Nodding in her voice. Soft and certain at once — she's been holding this memory for decades. Slight upward lift at 'don't you dear?' like she's inviting him into the shared certainty.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、お酢の、絶対、酸性、絶対、お料理、絶対、よく、絶対、作ったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how often you'd cook with vinegar — making those dishes so carefully. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Quieter this time, more inward. The memory feels more precious because it's smaller. Trailing off slightly, letting the image settle between them.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、バニラ、絶対、香りの、絶対、ケーキ、絶対、好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how much your father loved that vanilla-scented cake. You remember that, don't you dear?
lines.style: Brighter than before — a small smile in the voice. Not quite lifting the weight, but acknowledging something joyful underneath it. Warm and present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ともだち、絶対、皆と、絶対、よく、絶対、釣りに行ったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how you'd go fishing with your father and all his friends. You remember that, Gran?
lines.style: Leaning forward slightly in his posture. More direct now. The affection is clearer. He's asking her to confirm the shared joy of it, not just the fact.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、オールスター、絶対、戦、絶対、テレビで、絶対、応援していたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how you used to cheer for the Giants during the All-Star games on television. You remember that, don't you dear?
lines.style: Lifting a little — there's something lighter in this memory. Playful nostalgia. The voice settles comfortably, like she's smiling at the thought of him as a young man.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ジャイアンツ、絶対、応援、絶対、ずっと、絶対、続けてきたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how you've always supported the Giants — kept that support going all these years. You remember that, Gran?
lines.style: Steadier, more grounded. A note of quiet pride underneath — acknowledging something consistent about her, something that has lasted. Gentle but clear.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、英語、絶対、ペラペラ、絶対、と、絶対、お話、絶対、できたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, I remember how fluently you could speak English — the way you talked was so clear. You remember that, don't you dear?
lines.style: Tender, almost marveling. The voice softens on 'fluently.' He's not asking if she remembers — he's expressing quiet admiration. Close and intimate, like he's speaking only to her.
